statement: Three printers each work at a steady rate. Printers A and B together finish a job in 6 hours, B and C together in 10 hours, and A and C together in 7 hours 30 minutes. How long would all three together take to finish the same job?

choices.misconception: I added the three pair rates to get 2/5 of the job per hour but forgot that this counts every printer twice.
I took the time of the fastest pair, thinking the third printer would add very little.
I averaged the three times, 6, 10 and 7.5 hours, as if times could be averaged like rates.
I added the three times and halved, 23.5/2, applying the counted-twice idea to times instead of rates.

hints: Work with jobs per hour, not hours per job.

Write each pair's rate as a fraction of the job per hour. Adding all three pair rates counts each printer exactly twice, so halve the total to get the three-printer rate, then turn it back into a time.
The pair rates are 1/6, 1/10 and 2/15 of the job per hour.

solutions.reliable: In jobs per hour, a + b = 1/6, b + c = 1/10 and a + c = 1/7.5 = 2/15. Adding these, 2(a + b + c) = 5/30 + 3/30 + 4/30 = 12/30 = 2/5, so a + b + c = 1/5 and all three together take 5 hours. Check: the single rates are a = 1/10, b = 1/15 and c = 1/30, and 1/10 + 1/15 = 1/6 as required. The transferable idea: rates add but times do not; convert to rates, combine, and convert back.
solutions.elegant: Imagine 30 hours of work. A and B would finish 5 jobs, B and C 3 jobs, and A and C 4 jobs: 12 jobs in all, which is the work of two copies of all three printers. So the three together finish 6 jobs in 30 hours, one job every 5 hours.

whyOnTest: Combined-work problems test whether you add rates rather than times, and each distractor is a way of adding or averaging the times instead.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
